paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's rest is still on the table. The writer of Hebrews says "There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God" (Hebrews 4:9). The people in the wilderness heard the same good news we did, but it did them no good because they did not share the faith of those who understood it (Hebrews 4:2). So the question for you is not whether the promise is real. It's whether you'll believe it.

And notice the word the writer keeps pointing at: "Today." God spoke through David and said, "Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts" (Hebrews 4:7). Friend, I know how it feels to put things off, and I have NEVER once regretted doing the thing when I heard the call. The writer says to "make every effort to enter that rest" (Hebrews 4:11), and the reason is so no one falls by following the same pattern of disobedience. Resting in God means you stop leaning on your own work, just as God rested from His (Hebrews 4:10).

Why can you trust all this? Because "the word of God is living and active," and it "judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart" (Hebrews 4:12). Nothing is hidden from God's sight, and He is the One to whom we must give account (Hebrews 4:13). I think that sounds heavy, but it also means you can stop pretending, because He already sees all of you. So come to the Word with an open heart, listen today, and rest.
